description: Decide which comments belong in the source code you are writing or changing, and word them, following The Art of Readable Code (Boswell & Foucher). Every code change is also a set of comment decisions, and the usual defaults are wrong: comments that restate the line below, comments that narrate the edit ("added null check", "fixed the bug"), a header that repeats the signature, an invented reason next to a constant, an old comment left contradicting the new code. Use this skill whenever you write or modify code in any language — implementing a feature, fixing a bug, refactoring, writing a script or a test — even when the user never mentions comments, and before handing the change back. Also use it for "comment this code", "add docstrings", "clean up these comments", "are these comments any good".
